rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to maximize the chance of observing all 10 compounds and reveal the retention range and critical separations. The moderate gradient duration leaves ample time for late compounds to elute during the final hold.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing whether the current resolution margin is sufficient. Keeping temperature and endpoints fixed makes the effect of gradient steepness easier to assess.
Test temperature selectivity while retaining the fast gradient and its zero time penalty. Raising temperature may separate the crowded middle peaks without requiring a longer gradient.

Slightly lengthen the gradient to improve the remaining critical separation at 55 C while likely retaining a zero time penalty. Monitor the neighboring middle peaks as well, since their selectivity may shift with gradient duration.

The maximum CRF has already been reached; test a slightly shallower gradient for a nearby equally scoring method. Lowering phi1 to 0.90 may improve the 1.59-resolution pair while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty window, though the 1.52-resolution pair needs monitoring.

Test whether higher temperature improves the narrow critical-pair resolution margin while retaining the maximum CRF and zero time penalty. Injection 4 remains the established optimum if this selectivity change compromises another separation.

Return to 55 C and test a higher starting organic fraction to alter selectivity in the crowded middle region while maintaining a short elution time. This explores whether the maximum CRF can be retained with a larger critical-pair resolution margin.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness to improve the 1.29-resolution pair while preserving the favorable separation of the neighboring critical pair. The last peak should remain within the zero-time-penalty window, offering another candidate for CRF 1.000.

Continue the modest reduction in gradient steepness to bring the 1.47-resolution pair above 1.5 while retaining separation of the other critical pair. Extrapolation suggests the last peak will elute near 8 minutes, potentially preserving the zero time penalty.

Test a shifted, narrower gradient window to rebalance the two critical separations while keeping the last peak near 8 minutes. The maximum CRF is already established; this run explores whether a different starting composition can provide a larger minimum-resolution margin.

Test the lower-temperature side of the promising 55 C region while holding injection 8's gradient fixed. Cooling may improve its 1.47-resolution pair, but the neighboring critical separation must be checked for a competing loss in selectivity.

Preserve injection 4's successful gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint and shortening the programmed gradient. Because all peaks previously eluted before this gradient would end, their separations should remain unchanged, retaining CRF 1.000 with a lower final organic fraction.

Use a gradient slope between injections 8 and 9 to balance the two critical separations. This should retain CRF 1.000 while eluting the last peak slightly earlier than injection 9 and maintaining a modest resolution margin.

With the maximum CRF already secured, explore a lower-temperature selectivity regime using the fast scouting gradient. Cooling may separate the middle peaks on the opposite side of their apparent elution-order crossover, potentially yielding an alternative optimum with larger resolution margins.

Explore the opposite side of the high-temperature co-elution region using a higher starting organic fraction and shorter gradient. This may restore separation after an elution-order reversal while keeping the time penalty at zero; the established CRF 1.000 methods remain the benchmarks.

Increase the starting organic fraction to test whether the reversed middle pair separates further at 60 C while retaining rapid elution. Monitor the first two peaks closely, since their resolution may become limiting as initial retention decreases.

Test a steeper gradient at the starting composition that preserved early-peak resolution in injection 15. This may widen the reversed critical pair enough to reach maximum CRF with faster elution, although compression of neighboring separations must be checked.

Test an intermediate low-temperature regime with a moderately shallow gradient to seek an alternative selectivity window. This avoids the severe crowding observed at 25 C while probing whether the middle-peak order changes can yield full resolution without a substantial time penalty.

Return to the established optimal temperature and slightly flatten injection 9's gradient to explore the resolution plateau. The observed trends suggest both critical separations can remain above 1.5 while the last peak stays within the demonstrated zero-time-penalty range.

Test whether a shallower gradient corrects injection 10's limiting separation while retaining its improved resolution of the other critical pair. This may increase the minimum-resolution margin, although later elution could introduce a time penalty; the established CRF 1.000 methods remain optimal.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 20 to improve its limiting separation and balance the two critical pairs near R = 1.7. The last peak is expected around 9.5 minutes, potentially retaining the maximum CRF with a larger resolution margin.

Set the gradient slope between injections 20 and 21 to balance the two critical separations near R = 1.7. This should preserve the maximum CRF while slightly reducing the last-peak retention time relative to injection 21.

Use nearly the same gradient slope as injection 22 with a shorter programmed gradient and lower final organic fraction. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends, preserving CRF 1.000 and approximately 1.7 minimum resolution.

Preserve injection 4's successful gradient slope while shortening the programmed gradient to 8 minutes and lowering the endpoint. Since all peaks previously eluted before the new gradient would finish at the outlet, this should retain CRF 1.000 and the 7.60-minute last-peak time.

Preserve injection 9's gradient slope and temperature with a shorter programmed gradient and lower endpoint. Its last peak eluted at 8.00 minutes, before this gradient ends at the outlet at 8.65 minutes, so CRF 1.000 and minimum resolution near 1.58 should be retained.
